title: Kernel auto-selection v2 — rollout retro (runtime-1.19)
body:
Kernel auto-selection v2 — rollout retro (runtime-1.19)
Owner: Talia Benson (Program Mgmt)
Retro date: 2026-02-20
Last updated: 2026-02-24

Attendees (core): Grace Kim, Yuki Sato, Omar El-Sayed, Lena Fischer, Connor O’Brien, Aisha Bello, Thomas Baird, Anika Gupta, Sana Farid

Scope / what we’re retro-ing
- Feature: selector v2 (table-driven kernel registry + rule fallback) shipped with runtime-1.19
- Rollout: internal canary → hosted 5% (us-east) → hosted 25% → dedicated opt-in (limited) → default-on (paused before full default-on)
- Focus: performance outcomes (p50/p95 latency + tok/s variance by GPU), correctness (NaN/shape mismatch), observability/monitoring, rollout process.

High-level outcome
- We achieved the intended direction: selection decisions became explicit + inspectable, and variance across GPU SKUs improved for the “mainline” model families (Llama/Mistral) on A100/H100.
- We did not meet the bar for a clean, low-drama rollout: we hit (1) a p95 regression on A10 long-context decode, (2) a correctness scare with NaNs for a narrow shape/kernel combo, and (3) excessive metrics cardinality early in canary.
- Net: rollout paused at 25% hosted while fixes landed; dedicated opt-in remained available with clear override/kill-switch guidance.

What went well
1) Table-driven registry + deterministic behavior
- Having a registry row per {model family x seq bucket x GPU class} reduced “mystery” behavior; when we regressed, we could point to a specific entry (or missing entry).
- Deterministic tie-breaking and stable bucketing made perf comparisons much easier than v1 heuristics.

2) Fast iteration loop between benchmark-lab → canary → fix
- Benchmark sweep caught the seq-bucket boundary bug before broad default-on (PR: pr_18571_fix_seq_bucket_off_by_one).
- Canary surfaced an A10-specific tail regression that benchmark-lab didn’t reproduce at first; once we aligned prompt distribution + batching settings, we could reproduce and validate the registry change.

3) Rollback and overrides worked in practice
- The kill switch behaved as designed and prevented extended customer impact.
- Per-model-family override was used successfully for a Dedicated evaluation request (SUP-8860 context) without requiring a runtime rollback.

4) Conformance testing changed team behavior (good)
- The NaN incident forced us to treat “correctness regressions” as first-class gates, not “we’ll keep an eye on it.”
- Anika’s conformance suite additions created a repeatable checklist for future kernel registry changes.

5) Cross-team coordination improved after the first canary incident
- Once we adopted a single “rollout checklist + dashboards to watch” doc and pinned it in the release channel, comms got materially better (less duplicated triage, fewer contradictory next steps).

What didn’t go well (and contributing factors)
1) Canary p95 regression on A10 for long-context workloads
- Symptom: p95 latency increase concentrated on A10 when effective context > ~4k and decode-heavy prompts (see Slack thread 1737398821_900114).
- Root cause (most likely): an initial registry choice favored a kernel that looked better on short context / prefill but had worse cache behavior + batching interaction in long decode on A10.
- Contributing factors:
  - Benchmark prompt distributions underrepresented “decode-heavy long tail” for A10.
  - We didn’t have a clear “A10 long-context guardrail” threshold at the perf-canary gate level.

2) Correctness scare: sporadic NaNs
- Symptom: sporadic NaNs reported internally and later echoed by a customer ticket (SUP-8874) with limited reproduction info.
- Root cause: one kernel path appears numerically unstable for a narrow combination of head dim / GQA setting / seq bucket under certain compiler flags (still under investigation; mitigation is exclusion from safe set + conformance coverage).
- Contributing factors:
  - “Safe kernel set” policy existed but was not strict enough in initial registry promotion.
  - Conformance suite initially focused on shape compatibility; we added stronger NaN/overflow guards after the incident.

3) Metrics cardinality blow-up early in canary
- Symptom: selector telemetry increased time series count more than expected; dashboards became laggy and some alerts were delayed/noisy.
- Root cause: label combinations included too-granular kernel identifiers and model names before bucketing/normalization (PR: pr_18519_reduce_metric_cardinality_for_kernel_choice).
- Contributing factors:
  - We treated telemetry standards as “final hardening” rather than pre-canary requirement.
  - No pre-canary “cardinality budget” review with a concrete check (we had a meeting, but not an automated verification).

4) Unknown model family fallback bug
- Symptom: rare crash in canary for a model that lacked complete metadata; the fallback path didn’t properly route to safe kernel set.
- Fix: PR pr_18526_fix_unknown_model_family_fallback_bug.
- Contributing factors:
  - We didn’t have a dedicated test fixture for partial/unknown metadata in the selection context.
  - We overestimated how often model metadata is “complete and clean” in production.

5) Release comms: “is it safe to proceed?” ambiguity
- During the first rollback decision, there was confusion on who makes the call and what exact thresholds triggered rollback.
- After we aligned with SRE on explicit rollback criteria, execution improved (but this should have been done before enabling 5%).

Monitoring + observability gaps (specific)
1) We lacked an at-a-glance view that correlated “selector decision” → “latency impact” by GPU and seq bucket
- We had each component separately (selector version breakdown, latency charts, GPU breakdown), but not a single panel that tells you: “A10 + long-decode + kernel X is regressing.”
- Action: add a heatmap panel keyed by {gpu_class, seq_bucket, kernel_choice_bucket} with overlaid p95 delta vs control.

2) We didn’t have a clear “correctness early warning” metric
- Error rates didn’t move; NaNs showed up as quality/correctness issues not well captured by standard 5xx.
- Action: add NaN/Inf detection counters (sampled) at a low overhead point in the runtime output checks, plus trace annotation for flagged requests.

3) Sampling strategy not clearly documented
- Confusion during triage: were traces representative, or did sampling bias hide the long-context population?
- Action: document sampling + ensure long-context buckets get minimum sampling rate during rollout windows.

4) Canary analysis playbook was too implicit
- Sana had to manually remind everyone which comparisons matter (control vs treatment, by GPU SKU, by seq bucket, excluding warmup).
- Action: publish a “canary analysis template” with a repeatable query set.

Process improvements (agreed)
- Promote telemetry/cardinality review to a Phase-1 deliverable (pre-canary), not a follow-up.
- Require “unknown/partial metadata” tests for any selector logic change.
- For registry changes that affect A10/L4 specifically, require a targeted benchmark run with decode-heavy long-context prompts.
- Tie rollout stages to explicit sign-offs:
  - Runtime owner (Hiro/Grace delegate)
  - SRE owner (Aisha delegate)
  - Release owner (Connor)

Timeline notes (condensed)
- runtime-1.19 cut + internal canary: smooth; debug endpoint helped several times.
- Hosted 5% us-east: discovered A10 long-context p95 regression → rollback.
- Fixes landed: seq bucket boundary bug fix + A10-specific registry tweak + telemetry cardinality reduction.
- Hosted 25%: stable for A100/H100; continued watch on L4/A10; paused before default-on pending correctness confidence improvements.

Action items / follow-up backlog
(Tracking note: some of these are new follow-ups; others map to existing tickets. Owners listed are directly responsible for driving to closure.)

P0 — correctness / safety
1) Expand conformance suite to include NaN/Inf checks per kernel choice + shape set
- Owner: Anika Gupta
- Due: 2026-03-06
- Notes: must run in CI nightly + on registry promotion; include at least one GQA-heavy model shape.

2) “Safe kernel set” policy enforcement
- Owner: Grace Kim
- Due: 2026-03-01
- Notes: add a registry validation rule: any new entry must reference either (a) safe set, or (b) explicitly documented exception with conformance evidence.

P0 — monitoring
3) Add NaN/Inf runtime counters + trace annotations (sampled)
- Owner: Omar El-Sayed
- Due: 2026-03-08
- Notes: keep labels minimal; tie into telemetry standards.

4) Dashboard: selector decision heatmap + p95 deltas by GPU + seq bucket
- Owner: Aisha Bello
- Due: 2026-03-10
- Notes: integrate into standard runtime perf dashboard; include link from rollout checklist.

P1 — performance guardrails
5) Add A10/L4 long-context decode distribution to benchmark-lab default matrix
- Owner: Rina Kobayashi (FYI; not present today)
- Due: 2026-03-15
- Notes: ensure the prompt distribution includes decode-heavy and mixed batching conditions.

6) Perf-canary: explicit guardrail thresholds by GPU class
- Owner: Sahana Iyer (FYI)
- Due: 2026-03-12
- Notes: require separate budgets for A10 and L4; avoid “blended p95 hides SKU regression.”

P1 — telemetry/cardinality discipline
7) Add pre-canary “cardinality budget check”
- Owner: Thomas Baird
- Due: 2026-03-05
- Notes: lightweight script or dashboard check that estimates series explosion from label sets; gate rollout if above budget.

P2 — productization / ops
8) Improve override runbook clarity + precedence examples
- Owner: Kira Thompson (FYI)
- Due: 2026-03-18
- Notes: include 3 examples: disable v2 globally; pin kernel for model family; emergency safe-set only.

9) Registry promotion process: ownership + review checklist
- Owner: Yuki Sato
- Due: 2026-03-20
- Notes: propose “GPU owner review” requirement when changing entries for a GPU class.

Open questions (parked)
- Do we want to surface selector version / kernel choice in customer-facing Console for Dedicated? (PM-611 adjacent)
- How strict should “unknown model family” handling be: always safe set vs allow heuristics if metadata incomplete?

Decisions captured
- We will not proceed to default-on for all hosted regions until (a) NaN instrumentation is live and (b) A10/L4 guardrails exist in perf-canary and benchmark-lab.
- Selector telemetry labels must remain bucketed; raw kernel ids are allowed only in traces/logs (sampled), not as high-cardinality metric labels.

Notes to self / cleanup
- This doc should be linked from the rollout checklist and the runtime-1.19 release notes for internal context.
- Talia: schedule a 30-min follow-up in ~3 weeks to confirm action items landed and unblock default-on decision.
